solutions.check: 32 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 31 answers the paper printed; printed-crossing fills: 22-down

clue.text: A picture of vessels returning gunfire

indicators.note: returning means the word for vessels is read back to front

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels
a shot is a single discharge of gunfire

explanation.surface: A photograph of ships coming home under a salvo of gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick informal photograph is a snapshot, so it is one kind of picture.

clue.text: The _____ on Whitehall gate looked forth into the night" (Macaulay)

definitions.text: The _____ on Whitehall gate looked forth into the night" (Macaulay)

parts.words: The _____ on Whitehall gate looked forth into the night" (Macaulay)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Macaulay's poem The Armada, where a watchman guarding the gate spots the warning beacons

explanation.surface: A line from Macaulay with one word missing, about a guard watching through the night.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government offices; the gap is the guard who watches, and the word fits anyone keeping watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard standing watch at a gate is a sentry, which is what the missing word means.

clue.text: The waiter, a sober worker, receiving a tip

indicators.note: receiving means the first group of pieces takes the word for tip inside it

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so sober
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords
the end of something is its tip

explanation.surface: A waiter who does not drink takes a gratuity from a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a gratuity left for the waiter, but it means the end of something; TT is the crossword shorthand for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who waits on or serves others is an attendant.

clue.text: Blacken and burn round the top of the meadow

indicators.note: round says the word for burn wraps around the letter that follows

parts.note: to sear is to burn or scorch

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Fire scorches the grass at the upper end of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear someone is to blacken their name by slander.

clue.text: Shady dealer's crime

parts.note: the possessive 's is read as the word of, standing in front of the receiver
a fence is a dealer in stolen goods

explanation.surface: The dishonest trader is guilty of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's is read as the word 'of' placed in front, a rare but fair device; a fence is criminal slang for a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime is a breach of the law, also called an offence.

clue.text: Flexible section of a gun-carriage

explanation.surface: A supple, movable part of an artillery carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Limber means supple or lithe; the limber is also the detachable two-wheeled front part of a field-gun carriage.

clue.text: Abuses till disconcerted over tears shed

indicators.note: disconcerted suggests the letters of till are thrown into disorder
shed as in scattered asks for the letters of tears to be spilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A shop till is thrown into confusion when tears are shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcerted' turns TILL into ILLT and 'shed' turns TEARS into REATS; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse someone is to treat them badly or cruelly.

clue.text: Intolerant guy made to move in a little

indicators.note: in puts the word for move inside the word for a little

parts.note: a bit is a little of something
a go is a move or turn in a game

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded man is made to shift over slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prejudiced who will not accept other views is a bigot.

clue.text: Still requiring an answer

explanation.surface: A question still awaits a response.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a glass vessel for distilling, a still; a retort is also a sharp reply.

clue.text: Shut up about Scripture — it's persuasive

indicators.note: about indicates the word for shut up surrounds the abbreviation for Scripture

parts.note: pent means confined or shut up
OT is the Old Testament, part of Scripture

explanation.surface: Confining a preacher to the Bible makes his sermons convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A potent argument is a powerful, convincing one.

clue.text: Not all would season it, rejecting salt

indicators.note: not all of these words is used, so the answer sits inside the run of letters across them

explanation.surface: A cook refuses to use salt, unwilling to season the dish at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like the thing being rejected, but it is the definition; the letters run across 'seasoN IT REjecting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, or potassium nitrate, is a chemical salt, the old name for which is nitre.

clue.text: A measure of illumination?

parts.note: read whimsically, a unit of length (as in a yard or an inch) followed by a word for brightness, as if naming a unit of lighting

explanation.surface: A question about how brightness is quantified.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lumen or candela; the question mark warns that the measure is a length unit placed beside a word for light, giving the row of lamps at the front of a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The row of lamps along the front edge of a theatre stage gives the actors their illumination.

clue.text: Car gone in for servicing — such innocence!

indicators.note: a car taken in for servicing is taken apart and put back together, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A naive motorist hands over a car for a service, trusting the garage entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for servicing' rearranges CARGONEIN, the letters of 'Car gone in'; 'such' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence can mean lack of knowledge or awareness, which is exactly what not knowing amounts to.

clue.text: A revolutionary piece of machinery, this

definitions.text: A revolutionary piece of machinery, this

parts.words: A revolutionary piece of machinery, this
parts.note: revolutionary is read as spinning round rather than radical, and the word for the part reads the same backwards as forwards, as if it too had been turned round

explanation.surface: An invention so radical it will change the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a ground-breaking invention; it means turning round, and the five-letter word is a palindrome, so it is unchanged when spun.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating part of an engine, helicopter or turbine is called the rotor.

clue.text: Question cut-back by colliery

indicators.note: back tells us the word for cut is written in reverse

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A question is raised about cutbacks at a coal pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-back' reads like one noun about spending cuts; split it, and 'back' is the reversal signal working on the word for cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone closely is to examine them, as a lawyer does a witness.

clue.text: Timetable — in time trains must follow it!

definitions.text: Timetable — in time trains must follow it!

parts.words: Timetable — in time trains must follow it!
parts.note: a planned route and schedule which travellers, and here the trains themselves, are meant to keep to

explanation.surface: A railway timetable that trains are expected to keep to.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation points to a timetable as a set route that must be followed, not a published list of departures.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned route or schedule of a journey is an itinerary.

clue.text: Left after trouble in the plant

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for left behind the word for trouble

parts.note: to tease someone is to trouble or pester them

explanation.surface: Someone is left behind after a spot of bother at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a prickly plant whose dried heads were once used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Reminiscent of English grammarian's case

parts.note: the vocative is the grammatical case used for addressing someone

explanation.surface: Something brings to mind an English grammar teacher's example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a briefcase or a legal case; to a grammarian it is a noun form.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative of a thing calls it to mind, so it brings back memories.

clue.text: In principle, soldiers qualify for housing

indicators.note: In says the soldiers go into the word for principle

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
men is the usual crossword word for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are entitled, in theory, to accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In principle' reads as 'theoretically'; split it, and 'In' is the container signal. 'qualify for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large building divided into flats or rooms for renting is a tenement, a form of dwelling.

clue.text: Everybody out to make a hit

explanation.surface: A union leader calls a walkout to land a blow on the bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a stoppage when all workers walk out; to strike is also to hit something.

clue.text: Invested, and owed in consequence

indicators.note: in puts the word for owed inside the word for consequence

parts.note: an end is an outcome or consequence
something due is owed

explanation.surface: Money was put in, and as a result is owed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' looks financial but means endowed, as with a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To be endued with a quality is to be endowed or clothed with it.

clue.text: Heartless rogue going to shop for refund

indicators.note: heartless strips away the inner letters of rogue, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: a store is a shop

explanation.surface: A cold-blooded crook goes back to a shop demanding his money back.
explanation.definitionFit: To refund is to give back, and to restore is likewise to return what was taken.

clue.text: Book for husband

explanation.surface: A wife books a table for her spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve a seat is to book it; to husband resources is to save or keep them back.

clue.text: Sack for taking money in general

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for money goes inside the word for general

parts.note: rife means general or widespread
L stands for pound (libra), British money

explanation.surface: A man is fired for pocketing cash among the general public.
explanation.walkthrough: L for a pound sterling comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, and to rifle a place is to ransack it for valuables.

clue.text: One getting caught up in father's problem

indicators.note: getting caught up in places the word for one inside the abbreviation for father

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone is drawn into a family difficulty with Dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A facer is a sudden setback or difficulty, a blow in the face.

clue.text: Playing as Perdita, quite incomparable

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played around with into a new order

explanation.surface: An actress in the role of Perdita, the heroine of The Winter's Tale, gives a peerless performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' looks like acting a part but rearranges ASPERDITA, the letters of 'as Perdita'.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are disparate are essentially different in kind, so they cannot be compared.

clue.text: A minor prize

parts.note: a ward is a minor under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A small trophy for a modest achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor' looks like 'small' describing the prize; it is a noun, a child in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize given in recognition of merit is an award.

clue.text: A youngster turning back can always appear a wrong 'un!

indicators.note: turning back means the young animal's word is written backwards

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior scout
taken as written
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A youth who goes astray can always end up looking like a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' reverses CUB to BUC; 'appear' is a link. A 'wrong 'un' is British slang for a bad character.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate who preyed on Spanish shipping was a buccaneer, which makes him a villain.

clue.text: A soldier the Continental finds quick-moving

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
le is the French for the, French being the Continental language here

explanation.surface: A European notices that a soldier is nimble on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone agile is nimble and able to move fast.

annotationWithheld.clue: Flowers nicely arranged, though it's a craft without appeal

clue.text: Steadier maybe, but most expeditious

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters of steadier may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A steadier approach might, oddly, also be the quickest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the letters of STEADIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The most ready is the quickest to act, so it is the most prompt or speedy.
